## Contract review

Inputs, and nothing else: card #11880 (body and all 11 comments, through the seat's answer `6067887446`); PR #12002 (body, its 10-file list, and the net diff against `main` at the merge-base `b13ea3c67f9c2b97066ac2c9f5524a2e3baafeac`); the 43 check-runs on this head. Read-only: the clone was fetched and read with `git show` / `git diff` / `git grep` only; nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Gate verdicts (the check-runs on the head):** 43 runs, 40 `success`, 3 `skipped` (the two coverage legs and `dependabot`), 0 failures. Among the successes: `Test` and all 8 shards, `Test (dist pins)`, `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Bundle Analysis`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Claim Re-read`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Overwrite Report`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Internal Docs Link Check`, `Doc Snippet Type Check`, `Doc Component Type Check`, `Doc Example Id Check`, `Doc Fence Language Check`, `README Export Check`, `Skill Example Check`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Docs Route Eager Closure Check`, `Pre-Install Import Graph Check`, `Inert vi.mock Specifier Check`, `Live E2E (informational)`. The diff touches none of the five `GOVERNED_SURFACES` the queue guard enumerates (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`).

**File surface against the claim `6066139411`:** the 10 files of the PR equal the net diff's stat. Runtime: `packages/components/src/renderers/basic/data-list.tsx`, `packages/types/src/zod/public-blocks.zod.ts`. Docs: `content/docs/guide/data-source.md`. Changeset: `.changeset/11880-repeater-datasource.md`. Tests: two new pins and four test-only edits. Every barred path is untouched: `block-config.ts` (a change there was the claim's stop), `PageBlockInspector.tsx`, `record-picker.tsx`, `elements.tsx`, `packages/i18n/**`, `packages/components/src/ui/**`, `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`, `zod/objectql.zod.ts`, `ObjectView.tsx`.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept sets, `@object-ui/types` (each checked against the arm in the diff, the sibling arms `ElementNumberBlockSchema` and `RecordLineItemsBlockArm` at the merge-base, and the spec's `ElementRepeaterPropsSchema` / `ElementDataSourceSchema` / `PageComponentSchema`):

1. **Strict face (`StrictAnyComponentSchema`) now ACCEPTS an `element:repeater` carrying `properties.object` plus a well-formed node-level `dataSource`** (it refused `unrecognized_keys` naming `dataSource`). RIGHT. `ElementRepeaterBlockSchema` declares `dataSource: stripImportedDefaults(SpecElementDataSourceSchema).optional()`, the one spelling the number and line-items arms already use; the spec's `PageComponentSchema` accepts the same node; the renderer now reads the key. This is the widening triage `6065828018` routed to the spec lane as `Clause-②: yes`, and the arm declares it by reference, as AGENTS.md #0.1 requires ("declare it on the node type that reads it, by reference to the spec row").
2. **Strict face now ACCEPTS a bag-less, binding-only repeater** (`type` plus `dataSource`, no `properties`), which it refused before as an unrecognized key. RIGHT, by the differential the new pin carries: the spec's `PageComponentSchema` accepts it and the row is judged only when a bag is present, as on every arm in the file (the `binding only, no bag` probe is pinned equal to the spec's verdict). The PR body names it openly (H2's addition). Consequence, stated not hidden: such a node renders one empty line per record (no `titleField`, no `fields`); that is an authoring-quality matter the spec itself admits, not a face defect.
3. **Strict and tolerant faces still REFUSE a bag without `object` beside a binding, at `properties.object` (`invalid_type`).** RIGHT. The spec row requires `object` ("without it the list never queries"), triage `6063784959` ruled A (no waiver in this step), and `held-public-block-arms-10872` keeps its assertion with only the title re-worded.
4. **Strict face still REFUSES a bogus node key beside the binding, and `dataSource` is not among the refused keys.** RIGHT (control pinned).
5. **Tolerant face (`safeValidateSchema`, `AnyComponentSchema` with `.passthrough()` at the node) now REFUSES a malformed `dataSource` on the repeater at `dataSource`** (a string, a non-string `object`, the undeclared member `objectName`, the record-form `filter`), where it passed any value through unjudged. RIGHT as a mirror: each of the four is refused by the spec's own `PageComponentSchema`, and the control is pinned beside every row. It is a NARROWING of a published accept set, so breaking for an author who validated through objectui's tolerant face alone; the changeset body spells it out. Carried into ② below.
6. **TypeScript authoring face: `PublicBlockNodeOf` for `'element:repeater'` gains optional `dataSource` typed as the spec's binding**, refusing `objectName` (the `@ts-expect-error` pin). RIGHT, additive, derived from the arm rather than hand-written.
7. The `zod-mirror-parity` EXCLUSIONS ledger row and the `DECLARES_DATA_SOURCE` set in `public-block-responsive-styles-10872` are re-worded / extended. RIGHT: forced bookkeeping with no accept-set effect of their own.

Public surface and behaviour, `@object-ui/components` (checked against `useElementDataSource`, `composeElementDataSource`, `useElementDataSourceSchema`, `mergeFilterNodes`, `toFilterNodeSafely` and `resolveFilterPlaceholders` at the merge-base):

8. **Registry manifest: `element:repeater` publishes the injected `dataSource` input** (`elementDataSourceBlock` marker, so `Registry.register` emits `ELEMENT_DATA_SOURCE_INPUT`); the four flat query inputs stay published and read, `object` stays `required: true` with its description saying a node-level `dataSource.object` wins. RIGHT: triage A keeps the flat keys until the v18 pin bump, and the spec row's requiredness is unchanged. The `MEMBER_PINS` row `element:repeater.dataSource` in `registry-inputs-spec-parity` is the manifest's required companion.
9. **A repeater bound only through `dataSource` lists its rows** (the card's first pin; it showed "No records"). RIGHT: `useElementDataSource(schema, adapter)` against the repeater's own adapter, as `ElementNumberRenderer` and `ElementRecordPickerRenderer` resolve theirs.
10. **A flat-only repeater reads exactly as before.** RIGHT: with no binding the hook answers `absent` and `composed` is undefined, so `object`, `sort` and `limit` fall to `props.*` and a lone filter passes verbatim to `useResolvedFilter`; the trailing `?? props.limit` keeps a flat non-usable cap behaving as it did (pre-existing, not a new rule). CONTROL pinned.
11. **Where a node carries both, the precedence is `ElementDataSourceGate`'s one table** (object: the binding's; filter: flat AND binding's, the binding's already ANDed with its view's; sort and limit: the binding's own, else the flat key, else the view's; a refused binding cap is not authored). RIGHT, checked member by member against `useElementDataSourceSchema`: `next[objectKey] = composed.object`; `mergeFilterNodes(own.node, bound.node)`; for sort `fromView = binding.config?.sort === undefined` and the component's key wins only over a view's; for limit `fromView = !isUsableRowLimit(binding.config?.limit)` and the component's usable cap wins only over a view's. The repeater's `config?.sort ?? props.sort ?? composed?.sort` and its `isUsableRowLimit` chain are that table. The dispatch's H1 wording ("the binding wins per member, the same precedence `element:number` had") was self-contradictory on `filter`; the dev measured it, the seat confirmed A in `6067887446`, and this review agrees independently.
12. **An unresolvable `view`, or a filter the two-source merge refuses, draws `ElementDataSourceErrorPanel` (`repeater-datasource-error`) and issues no read; a resolving view draws `ElementDataSourceLoadingPanel`.** RIGHT: `object` is `undefined` while `loading` / `missing` / refused, so the wider query the binding was written to narrow never fires; the same posture as `ElementNumberRenderer`, which also draws the error panel for a `filterRefusal`. Said exactly: only the two-source merge lowers through `toFilterNodeSafely`; a lone filter, flat or bound, passes verbatim as `element:record_picker` passes `composed.filter`, so the changeset's "a filter the merge refuses" is the precise wording.
13. **Context tokens survive the merge.** RIGHT: the merged result is an AST (`and` over two lowered nodes); `resolveFilterPlaceholders` walks arrays and plain objects, so a `{current_user_id}` inside a merged node still resolves (objectui#10666 holds in the both-keys case too).
14. **The data-invalidation bus is keyed on the resolved object**, so a write to the flat object beside a binding does not re-read the bound list. RIGHT, pinned both ways.
15. **Hook order** is stable: the binding hook, the `scoped` memo, `useFilterScope`, `useResolvedFilter`, `useDataInvalidation` and the fetch effect all precede the early returns. RIGHT.
16. **Docs.** The table row `element:repeater | object ✅ | view: filter / sort / limit | filter ✅ (AND properties.filter) | sort ✅ | limit ✅` is accurate: the repeater prints its own `titleField` / `fields`, so a view's columns and kind are not read, while its filter, sort and cap are (the view-baseline pin). The new paragraph's precedence sentences match the code; the two-element paragraph is re-scoped to `element:record_picker` and `element:number` by name; the JSON fence authors `properties.object` beside `dataSource.object`, the shape both faces accept. RIGHT.
17. The refusal text `ELEMENT_REPEATER_NEITHER_CHANNEL` and the arm's docblock now name the binding. RIGHT (text only). The local `isUsableRowLimit` is the repo's stated rule (a local restatement at each enforcing site, as `element-data-source.ts` and `ElementDataSourceGate.tsx` both say), not exported, so no one-authority collision.

Named wrong: none.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/11880-repeater-datasource.md`: `@object-ui/types: minor`, `@object-ui/components: patch`. No `major` (`Changeset Bump Policy` success; AGENTS.md 版本号策略). The 39-package fixed group releases at `minor`.
- **`@object-ui/types: minor` — RIGHT.** The strict face widens (①.1, ①.2): a `Clause-②: yes` change takes at least `minor` (the ruled exception). The tolerant face narrows (①.5): a breaking change, which objectui ships as `minor` with the break spelled out in the changeset body, and the body does ("is refused at `dataSource` where it was passed through unjudged"). Nit, non-blocking: the word "breaking" itself is absent, where the sibling entry from objectui#11989 wrote "Breaking for an author who…"; no objectui gate reads a banner.
- **`@object-ui/components: patch` — RIGHT**, on the card's own framing of item 1: a key the pinned spec already declared on the node and the renderer did not read ("renders No records"), consumption of a declared key rather than a new capability; a flat-only repeater reads byte-identically; the injected input is the manifest's statement of that read.
- **One changeset for three released packages' `src/`** (the third is `apps/console`'s test file): the presence gate asks for one declaration per change and a test-only change owes no bump. RIGHT (`Changeset Declaration` success).
- **`Clause-②:` line — RIGHT.** The PR body's third line reads `Clause-②: yes — …`, value first at the start of the line, and the direction is true: declaring `dataSource` on the arm widens `StrictAnyComponentSchema`'s accept set (triage `6065828018`, claim `6066139411`). It supersedes the first claim's `Clause-②: no` (`6062231663`), which the retriage corrected for the repeater half. Spelling nit, non-blocking: the diff also narrows the tolerant face, so the fuller spelling under `clause2-line.mjs` is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; an absent arm declares no direction and takes at least `minor` either way, the body text states the narrowing in full, and objectui runs no arm reader.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `6067844238` (one `open_questions` entry, five `deviations`, three `out_of_scope_findings`) and the PR body's acceptance notes, each answered or escalated:

1. **open_questions, precedence A or B** — ANSWERED A by the seat in `6067887446`; confirmed independently here (①.11). Ablations B and D in the PR body name the two pins that move under B. Closed.
2. **deviation (1), the same precedence** — closed with 1.
3. **deviation (2), three test files outside the claim's literal list** (`registry-inputs-spec-parity` under `apps/console`, `public-block-responsive-styles-10872`, `held-public-block-arms-10872`) — ACCEPTED: each is forced by the claimed change (the injected input needs its `MEMBER_PINS` row; the `DECLARES_DATA_SOURCE` set reddens on any arm gaining `dataSource`; a title said the repeater "never reads one"), all test-only, within "the tests beside these", and no barred path is touched.
4. **deviation (3), the union ran at `a7c1338e5` and the last commit changed only the new pin's mock typing** — moot: the check-runs on this head are the verdict, and they are green.
5. **deviation (4), the changeset lists two of the three counted packages** — judged in ②; closed.
6. **deviation (5), the PR opened at `a7c1338e5` and the head pushed after** — the body describes this head; its claims match the diff read here. Closed.
7. **out_of_scope (a) / acceptance note, the designer's `titleField` / `fields` pickers read `properties.object` while the renderer lists `dataSource.object` on a hand-written node naming two different objects** — ACCEPTED as noted, carrier objectstack#11509's spec half (the pin bump moves the repeater's designer rows). The claim barred `block-config.ts`, the designer never writes a repeater binding, and the docs tell an author to name the same object in the bag. Not escalated.
